title: VisualPrompter: Semantic-Aware Prompt Optimization with Visual Feedback for Text-to-Image Synthesis
claim: Generative models routinely fail to render key prompt concepts, and different models fail in different ways on the same prompt.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; image strips with colored prompt keywords matching model labels
description: Two-part figure with a row of generated images and a caption under each part. Panel (a), 'Typical failures of generative models', has three images, each with its prompt above and a failure label below. A beaver with glasses has no neck (red 'a neck', labeled 'Missing concept'). A kitchen lacks the 'modern art' backsplash (labeled 'Weak concept'). A cat sleeps on a laptop but does not hold the mouse (red 'holding', labeled 'Wrong concept'). Panel (b), 'Same prompt in different incorrect ways', shows one long prompt about a raccoon on a motorbike. Its key phrases are colored orange, green and blue. Three images come from SDXL, Flux-dev and Janus-pro, and the model names use the same colors. Each image misses different elements, such as the helmet, the dogs or the supplies. The eye goes first to the colored words and the photos.
caption: Existing T2I generative models often fail to correctly draw key concepts within the provided prompts. Different models also fail differently on the same prompt.
abstract: The notable gap between user-provided and model-preferred prompts poses a significant challenge for generating high-quality images with text-to-image models, compelling the need for prompt engineering. Current studies on prompt engineering can effectively enhance the style and aesthetics of generated images. However, they often neglect the semantic alignment between generated images and user descriptions, resulting in visually appealing but content-wise unsatisfying outputs. In this work, we propose VisualPrompter, a novel training-free prompt engineering framework that refines user inputs to model-preferred sentences. VisualPrompter utilizes an automatic self-reflection module that identifies absent concepts in the generated images, followed by a target-specific prompt optimization mechanism that revises the prompts in a fine-grained manner. By deconstructing prompts, introducing new elements at the atomic semantic level, and then reassembling them, our framework is able to maintain semantic consistency and integrity throughout the optimization process. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of VisualPrompter, which achieves new state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks for text-image alignment evaluation. Additionally, our framework features a plug-and-play design, making it highly adaptable to various generative models. Our code is available at https://github.com/teheperinko541/VisualPrompter.
